learning_outcomes.text: To gain knowledge about atomic structure, interatomic bonding, crystal structure of materials, diffusion in metals
Learning the engineering materials and their general properties
To gain theoretical knowledge and practical experience about mechanical tests of metallic materials
Gaining ability to analysis the mechanical test results
To design and control the heat treatment procedures
To understand the iron-carbon phase diagram and phase transformation in steels
To understand the relationship between microstructure and mechanical properties of engineering materials
To learn the general criteria about the material selection in product design

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Engineering Materials: Classissification, Metals, Ceramics, Polymers, Composites
The Structure of Crystalline Solids: Atomic arrangements and crystals, Imperfections in crystals, Microstructural examination of materials
The Structure of Crystalline Solids: Atomic arrangements and crystals, Imperfections in crystals, Microstructural examination of materials
Mechanical Testing and Properties: Tensile test, Hardness test, Fatigue test, Creep test, Impact test, Bending and Shear (Torsion), Wear and Corrosion test methods
Midterm Exam I: Mechanical Testing and Properties: Tensile test, Hardness test, Fatigue test, Creep test, Impact test, Bending and Shear (Torsion), Wear and Corrosion test methods
Iron-carbon phase diagrams and Heat treatments
Midterm Exam I: Iron-carbon phase diagrams and Heat treatments
bibliography: The Science and Engineering of Materials, D.R. Askeland
Materials Science and Engineering: An Introduction, W.D. Callister, 8th ed., John Wiley, 2007
